dedupe_keys.name: community level multi hazard resilience analysis using earthquake tsunami fragility surfaces and monte carlo simulation in the pseudo seaside testbed

description: Community-Level Multi-Hazard Resilience Analysis Using Earthquake-Tsunami Fragility Surfaces and Monte Carlo Simulation in the Pseudo Seaside Testbed is a dataset listed in DesignSafe Data Depot (published projects), a research data repository for natural hazards engineering under the section "simulation", published or maintained by John van de Lindt, Colorado State University (colostate.edu). This project presents a novel methodology for community-level resilience analysis under multi-hazard earthquake-tsunami scenarios by integrating 3D fragility surfaces with Monte Carlo simulation. Coverage: as described in the project (site or event named in the description). DesignSafe files it as a "simulation" project. Keywords: Community resilience, Multi-hazard analysis, Earthquake-tsunami fragility surfaces, Structural vulnerability, Seismic resilience, Tsunami impact assessment. Published 2025-02-12. It is reached through the links recorded on this page, with the catalogue entry as the discovery route. Access is free of charge and open. The licence is ODC-By-1.0. Caveats: this record was written from the catalogue listing only, so the linked page was not opened, its contents and current availability were not checked, and the description may lag the source. It can support structural performance, hazard exposure and resilience studies. Related record: the catalogue-level record data-designsafe-data-depot-repository.
